paragraphs.label: Μέρος Αʹ — Ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ (Part A — The Son of God)
paragraphs.translation: After a little while a certain woman comes from the village toward the spring. She has a water jar and comes in order to draw water from the spring.

Jacob rises up and greets her: "Peace to you, O woman. I am very thirsty, I and my donkey. But I do not have a water jar to draw the water. I see that you have a water jar. Are you able to draw and provide water for us from the spring so that we may drink?"
The woman says to him: "Peace to you, yes, O man. I am able to draw water for you. I give water to you and to your donkey."
So then the woman draws water in her jar and gives it to Jacob so that he may drink.
"I give thanks to you, O woman," says Jacob to her. Then he drinks the water and wants to give some to the donkey too; so he gives him water so that he may drink.

The woman says: "I see that you and your donkey give joy to each other; for you give him water, and he brings you the beautiful fruits and beautiful vegetables." And Jacob laughs and says: "Yes, we give to each other; this donkey of mine is good and strong. He always works with me because he is faithful."
After this the woman says: "What is your name?"
He answers: "My name is Jacob. And you, O woman, what is your name?"
She says to him: "My name is Salome."

Then Jacob opens his mouth and says: "I give thanks to you, O Salome, because you give me water so that I may drink and not be thirsty. Now my body is no longer thirsty. For bread is the food of the body, and water is the drink of the body. For whenever the body is hungry, we eat bread; and whenever it is thirsty, we drink water. But I know another food and another drink, and this is the food and drink of the spirit."
Salome marvels and says: "What are you saying? I do not understand. What is the food and drink of the spirit?"

Jacob answers her: "Listen, O Salome. A person has both body and spirit. With the body we eat bread and drink water, so that the body may live. With the spirit we know God and worship him, so that the spirit may live. Just as you give bread to the body, so God gives life to the spirit."
Salome says to him: "I still do not understand well."

Jacob says to her: "Do not worry; I speak to you slowly and carefully. And you will understand well. God is not like the sun or the earth. For he has no body. God is spirit. And we worship him in spirit and in truth. Whenever a person worships God in spirit and in truth, God hears him. This is the will of God."
Salome rejoices and says: "I know the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob. And I worship him."
Jacob says: "And I also believe and worship the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. But I give you something else."
Salome answers and asks Jacob: "What are you about to give me?"

Jacob answers and says: "Listen then, O Salome. I speak to you slowly and carefully. Just like you, I also believe and worship the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. But I tell you another word, and this word is great."
Salome [says]: "Tell me; I want to hear so that I may know about God."

Jacob is silent and looks at Salome, and after a little while he opens his mouth and says again: "This is the great word: Jesus is the Son of God. Yes, I truly say to you. Jesus is the Son of the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. For this reason I believe and follow Jesus. I am a disciple of Jesus and I love Jesus and I listen to Jesus because Jesus is the Christ."
Salome says to him: "Now I understand that you are a Christian. I know the God of Abraham, but I do not know Jesus well and precisely, nor do I believe in him. But tell me who exactly is this Jesus."

Jacob says to her: "Yes, you rightly understand that I am a Christian. For I believe in Jesus and I walk with Jesus and I listen to his voice. For I am a disciple of Jesus. And I tell you even more: Jesus is the bread of life."
Salome asks Jacob: "But what does it mean that Jesus is the bread of life? I do not understand; tell me so that I may know."

Jacob answers and says: "Listen; I tell you slowly and carefully so that you may know. Jesus is the bread of life. Whoever comes to him will no longer be hungry, and whoever believes in him will no longer be thirsty. Just as you give us water from the spring, so Jesus gives the water of life; and whoever drinks the water of life will not be thirsty again. But this food and drink of Jesus is of the spirit, not of the body."
Salome is silent and listens. She still has and carries her water jar, and the water is in it; but now she is concerned about the water of life.

paragraphs.label: Μέρος Βʹ — Ἡ Ἄμπελος ἡ Ἀληθινή (Part B — The True Vine)
paragraphs.translation: Jacob and Salome are still conversing with each other under the great tree in the shade. The sun is shining greatly and the heat still remains on the road and in the fields. So Salome takes the water jar again in order to draw water. For she wants to give more water to Jacob's donkey.

Jacob sets down his bag under the tree because he wants to rest more. For he does not want to travel in the heat. And Salome gives the water to the donkey so that he may drink. Then she places the water jar upon the stone under the tree.
After this they sit down again in the shade away from the heat of the sun. And Salome wants to hear more about Jesus.
She says then to Jacob: "Are you able to teach me more about Jesus? It pleases me to hear about Jesus and to learn."
Jacob answers: "Yes, I am able to speak to you about Jesus. And I rejoice that it pleases you to hear about Jesus. And I speak to you so that you may learn."

And Jacob looks at the fields around the spring, and he sees a vine near the road. The vine has many branches, and the branches bear much fruit. He says then: "Do you see that vine, which is near the spring? The vine has branches. And the branches, which remain in the vine, bear much fruit."
Salome answers: "Yes, I see."

"Listen, O Salome," he says. "If the branch remains in the vine, it bears fruit; but if it does not remain in the vine, it is not able to bear fruit. For apart from the vine the branch is nothing. And whenever the branch remains in the vine, it lives and grows and bears fruit; but whenever it does not remain, it does not grow but dies."
Salome looks at the vine and the branches. "This I understand," she says. "The branch lives and grows in the vine. But what does this say about Jesus?"
Jacob rejoices: "You ask well, O Salome. I say this because Jesus says: I am the true vine and my Father is the farmer."
Salome says: "But what does this mean?"

Jacob answers: "Yes!" he says. "Jesus is the true vine, and we Christians are the branches. If we remain in Jesus, we bear much fruit. But if we do not remain in him, we are not able to do anything; for apart from him we are not able to bear fruit, just as the branch [cannot] apart from the vine. For Jesus also says: I am the vine, you are the branches. The person who remains in me and I in him, he bears much fruit, because apart from me you are not able to do anything."
Salome marvels and asks Jacob: "But what happens if we do not remain in Jesus?"

Jacob says: "That is just like it is in the field; the farmer cuts off the branch from the vine which does not bear fruit, and throws it into the fire. But the branch which bears fruit, the farmer prunes it so that it may bear much fruit. If then we remain in Jesus and Jesus in us, we are able to bear much fruit and we live with joy and peace."
Salome answers: "Now I marvel that I have never known this. I only know about the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and David."
Jacob says: "Now you know that Jesus is the bread of life and the true vine."

Salome says: "But I also know that the Scripture teaches us that God is one. For it says: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one; and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength."

"Yes," says Jacob. "You know the Scriptures well and you speak rightly. It pleases me to hear this. But listen to me again. Jesus is the Son of God. God remains in Jesus and Jesus remains in God. Not only this, but Jesus also says this: I am the way and the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through me. For this reason we are only able to come to God the Father through Jesus, because Jesus is the way. And Jesus is the Christ, in whom we remain."
These words of Jacob stir up and disturb the heart of Salome.
